title: Experimental Stats Sorting and Protocol Analytics
summary: Coach Profiles can be ranked by any report metric, while Battle Visualizer protocol analytics now separates meaningful battle signals from raw transport noise.

changes.text: Added sortable Coach Profiles columns for coach, replay matches, win rate, damage, healing, setup, favorable events, and items, with reversible direction and unavailable values kept at the bottom.
Normalized Battle Visualizer protocol-event labels, removed transport, chat, timestamp, team-preview, and unknown lines from Event Density, and kept the complete raw stream searchable for audit.

title: Season 11 Backfill Runbook Fix
summary: The documented Fly maintenance commands now run with the production volume and record the completed historical backfill.

changes.text: Updated Fly SSH examples to pass environment variables through env and documented the verified Season 11 HAX and Mega-item backfill results, including intentionally unmatched legacy evidence.

title: Season 11 Production Backfill Path
summary: Existing Season 11 replay evidence can now be filled through a guarded, backup-first maintenance run.

changes.text: Added bundled backup, Season 11 favorable-event, and Mega Stone maintenance commands that use the production SQLite client and require explicit confirmation before writes.
Documented the controlled dry-run, backup, and quiet-window workflow while keeping backfills out of automatic application startup.

title: Experimental Stats Audit Fixes
summary: Experimental Stats deep links and week filters now fail more predictably.

changes.text: Removed a React SVG title warning in the Team Core Network, normalized reversed or out-of-range week selections, restricted dynamic report links to supported slugs, and added a mobile-safe clipboard fallback.

title: Metric Glossary Category Accents
summary: Metric Glossary sections are easier to scan while individual metric rows stay neutral.

changes.text: Added distinct, theme-aware category heading accents and side markers to the Metric Glossary for presentation and navigation clarity.

title: Experimental Stats Search Performance
summary: Visual Lab search stays responsive while filtered charts refresh.

changes.text: Deferred chart filtering and debounced shareable URL updates so report-wide searches remain responsive while typing.

title: Top Plays Pokémon Sprites
summary: Top Plays now makes Pokémon-specific moments easier to recognize at a glance.

changes.text: Added saved Pokémon sprites before latest-faint and longest-active record details when matching sprite evidence is available.

title: Team Stats Matchup Scope Context
summary: Team Stats now makes filtered matchup-side scope explicit.

changes.text: Added a scope note explaining that each row represents one team's side of the filtered matchup set and that coach or team searches retain opponents as separate comparison rows.

title: Favorable Event Context
summary: Signature Stats now explains its event-rate denominator and keeps replay-format differences visible.

changes.text: Bolded the Season(s), Apps, and Record scope columns and added a clear definition for favorable event coverage.

Expanded Season 11 Week 6+ parsing and backfill coverage for opponent-applied secondary effects, stat drops, and logged blocked status turns while preserving the legacy Seasons 5–10 and Season 11 Weeks 1–5 format.

title: Battle Visualizer Color Context
summary: Battle Visualizer box scores now use semantic color cues to make replay metrics easier to scan.

changes.text: Color-coded KOs, deaths, damage, healing, turns, team results, and item evidence in the Pokémon box score, with an inline legend and text labels for accessibility.

title: Replay Search Context
summary: Replay Search now makes its search scope, result units, and KO filter definition clear.

changes.text: Added Pokémon, Team, Coach, and All search scopes with Pokémon selected by default, plus match-count context for appearance-level results.
Renamed the kills filter to Minimum Pokémon KOs, capped it at six for standard 6v6 battles, and explained that it measures one Pokémon rather than both sides combined.

title: Leaderboard Qualification Context
summary: Experimental Stats Leaderboards now make their minimum-appearance rule explicit.

changes.text: Added a visible qualification note above the leaderboard table and a Replay Search link for lower-volume Pokémon or coach appearances.

title: Rolling Trends Readability
summary: Rolling Trends now gives its chart labels more room and stronger contrast.

changes.text: Rolling Trends metric names and axes now use larger, higher-contrast typography with extra label room on responsive layouts.

title: Experimental Stats Compare Context
summary: Compare now focuses on useful side-by-side evidence, with common items and a clear Favorable Events definition.

changes.text: Removed the redundant Most-used move summary from the Compare scope.
Added per-Pokémon common-item summaries with item-data coverage, unknown/revealed counts, and inferred Mega Stone labels.
Added inline Favorable Events context plus a glossary link explaining which recorded outcomes count and how missing fields are handled.

title: Experimental Stats Coach and Move Context
summary: Coach Profiles now explain replay coverage and tendencies, while Visual Lab Move Usage is easier to search and read.

changes.text: Coach Profiles now explain recorded battle-length coverage, summarize replay-backed tendencies, and group item evidence with inferred Mega Stone context.
Visual Lab Move Usage is now a searchable vertical ranking with a top-15 default and a Show all control.

title: Experimental Stats Grouped Navigation
summary: The Experimental Stats landing page now groups reports by purpose so visitors can move from team performance to Pokémon analysis, trends, replay evidence, and reference material.

changes.text: Landing cards are organized into Team and league performance, Pokémon performance, Patterns and trends, Replay evidence, and Specialized reports and reference groups.
Each group has a labeled heading, short explanation, subtle category accent, and a consistent mobile stacking order.

title: Experimental Stats Mobile and Theme Polish
summary: Experimental Stats reports now fit narrow screens, explain swipeable content, and provide consistent touch and light/dark theme feedback.

changes.text: Dense report tables stay inside touch-scroll regions with swipe guidance, and mobile selectors, profile tabs, charts, and usage rows fit the available width.
Buttons, links, and selectors provide a brief pressed-state response on touch devices.
Experimental Stats muted labels now inherit theme-aware colors so light mode remains readable while dark mode keeps its existing contrast.

title: Experimental Stats Search Input Fix
summary: The report-wide Experimental Stats search field now keeps typed text while the URL scope updates.

changes.text: Search input state now syncs from URL changes only, so typing no longer gets overwritten by an in-flight router update.

title: Experimental Stats, Replay Evidence & Homepage Follow-up
summary: Experimental Stats now has clearer search, coverage, roster, Mega item, and report context, while the homepage Upcoming Battles panel is full width and localized.

changes.text: Added a report-wide search bar, sortable Pokémon and Team Stats columns, team-versus-global usage context, replacement and drop history, clearer setup-move definitions, and expanded coverage guidance.

Top Plays now ranks latest faint turns, Move Usage uses a searchable vertical ranking, Signature Stats shows real sprites, protocol-event gaps explain missing coverage instead of displaying misleading zeroes, and Coach Style Radar was removed.

Mega formes are preserved during replay parsing, matching Mega Stones can be inferred from historical roster context, contradictory item evidence flags a match for review, and a dry-run-by-default backfill command is available.
The Battle Visualizer links to the selected replay, average battle length uses saved timeline/event evidence, and Coach Profiles distinguish official records from replay-backed metrics.
Upcoming Battles now spans the full homepage width with aligned team logos, clearer playoff badges, and times shown in each visitor's local timezone.

title: Experimental Stats Audit Improvements
summary: Experimental Stats is lighter, clearer, and easier to verify through improved coverage rules, expandable Top Plays, report-linked definitions, and saved-turn evidence.

changes.text: Indirect-only damage is now recognized as recorded coverage, team reports retain both teams from qualifying matches, and compact grouped replay-event counts replace oversized raw event payloads.
Pokemon Profiles explain advanced metrics, show covered-sample qualification, and link directly to their glossary definitions.
Top Plays supports expandable rankings, one record per match, and links from recorded moments to their saved Battle Visualizer turn evidence.
Glossary search now includes visuals, reports a clear empty state, and links available definitions to the reports that use them.
Experimental charts initialize with stable dimensions, and every current report route is included in the public sitemap.

title: Experimental Stats Visual Lab
summary: Experimental Stats now has a deeper, filter-aware Visual Lab with source context, calculation guidance, and smoother chart updates.

changes.text: Added signature, team, top-play, momentum, move-usage, season/division, coach-style, coverage, and team-core visual reports.
Chart points, replay selectors, tables, lists, and exports now expose relevant season, division, week, team, coach, record, coverage, and replay context.
Shared Experimental Stats filtering uses deferred, memoized updates so filter controls stay responsive while expensive chart aggregations refresh.
Top-play charts now display their HP-swing, comeback-deficit, and active-appearance calculation guidance with accurate recorded-play axis labels.

title: PokéBase-Inspired Usage Reports
summary: Experimental Stats now includes a replay-backed Pokémon usage overview, configurable trends, qualified leaderboards, and clearer evidence coverage.

changes.text: Added a Pokémon usage overview with usage rate, win rate, team-appearance samples, weekly trends, common teammates, and supporting match evidence links.
Added three-, five-, and ten-game rolling windows, preset Pokémon and coach leaderboards, and CSV exports for the visible report.
Replay Search now supports text, minimum-damage, minimum-kill, and survived-battle filters, while Battle Visualizer replay selection remains shareable through the match query.
Reports expose field coverage and require at least three qualifying games for profiles and rankings; missing saved fields remain unknown instead of being treated as zero.

title: Lean Experimental Stats Reports
summary: Experimental Stats now sends large replay timelines only to reports that use them, making common reports lighter to load.

changes.text: Pokemon, Coach, Compare, Trends, Leaderboard, and Replay Search reports skip unused HP timeline and key-event JSON while Insights, Visualizer, Rare Events, and comeback rankings retain the evidence they need.

title: Reliable Power Rankings Slideshow Navigation
summary: Power Rankings slides now wait for their images and ignore overlapping clicks so every team card renders with the right sprites.

changes.text: Preloaded slide artwork, stable slide remounts, and transition locking prevent rapid clicks from showing stale or missing Pokemon images.

title: Schedule Match Stats Fit Their Cards
summary: Expanded Pokemon results remain readable without spilling beyond the schedule card.

changes.text: Long team and Pokemon names now shrink within the expanded schedule view while sprites and K/D totals remain fully visible on both sides.

title: Faster Planning, Search, and Statistics Pages
summary: Six no-cost code optimizations reduce repeated database work and the amount of data sent to several frequently used pages.

changes.text: Draft Planner sends repeated move names once and reconstructs learnsets in the browser, making its initial response substantially smaller.
Site search reuses a short-lived Pokemon index, runs independent lookups together, and cancels obsolete requests while a user keeps typing.
Matchup Prep loads prices only for the selected season instead of retrieving every historical price row.
Pokemon leaderboards now let the database calculate totals instead of loading every appearance into the application.
Coach profiles limit placement and playoff lookups to that coach's divisions and reuse store-purchase data.
Frequently read feature settings use a brief shared cache that is cleared immediately after an admin changes a setting.

title: Coach and Season Directory Performance
summary: Coach records and the season archive perform less unnecessary data loading and processing.

changes.text: Coach record filters reuse their team and match lookups, and the directory skips unfinished games and a redundant season lookup.
The season archive loads a total for each division instead of retrieving every historical team to count them.

title: Experimental Stats Full Audit
summary: Experimental Stats reports are better organized, easier to interpret, and synchronized with their filters and replay evidence.

changes.text: Insights is now its own report, each page has a collapsible report filter area, and Pokémon and coach qualification requires at least three appearances.
Added KO Differential, KO Differential/Game, and Move Usage leaderboard presets, sortable Career and Splits tables, and Regular Season versus Playoffs controls.
How-to-read guidance now explains first-faint advantage, coach shift, move-to-KO signals, battle momentum, replay pace, evidence coverage, and other unfamiliar metrics.
Replay-backed reports now show clearer matchup, coach, team, item, and source-game context, with alphabetical Pokémon selectors and the full word appearances.
Corrected coach match counts, damage-per-game and stage comparisons, comeback attribution, survival-rate bounds, held-item evidence, rare-event coverage, and protocol values.
The Battle Visualizer and Event Analytics now stay on the selected match, while replay pace uses a fuller 2-by-2 summary and report payloads avoid unnecessary timeline data.

title: Experimental Stats Replay Links
summary: Experimental stat tables now explain team attribution, connect item usage to source games, and make replay evidence easier to review.

changes.text: Item Impact rows now link directly to the season and week of every saved source match, with compact links that remain usable on smaller screens.
KO Conversion and Team Damage Share now credit each Pokémon to the team name that used it instead of aggregating records without team context.
Experimental stats navigation, sortable leaderboards, replay evidence labels, and Mega Evolution item handling are clearer and easier to audit.

title: Playoff Hub & Full-Bracket Pick-Ems
summary: A dedicated postseason hub, full-bracket predictions, spoiler controls, and more responsive playoff pages make the complete playoff experience easier to follow.

changes.text: Added a Playoff Hub with postseason-only KO, differential, MVP, and usage leaderboards plus a historical bracket archive.
Added persisted full-bracket Pick-Ems alongside weekly round picks, with progression validation, quarterfinal locking, and a separate leaderboard.
Playoff results start hidden on every visit during an active season, while completed seasons remain visible by default.
Playoff brackets and prediction cards use space more efficiently, show full names, expose actions without hover, and stack cleanly on mobile.
Moved Playoff Hub into the Seasons menu and added a homepage shortcut whenever the current playoff matchups are active.
Historical archives omit unavailable Season 3–5 promotion claims and do not claim Stargazer promotion before Season 11.

title: Clear Promotion & Relegation Rules
summary: Playoff pages now show the correct division movement rules and promotion paths.

changes.text: Replaced the blanket finalists-promote badges with the correct two-up or three-up movement for each current PBO division.
Added a promotion and relegation guide covering regular-season leaders, playoff qualifiers, relegation counts, and overlapping promotion spots.

title: Pokemon Image Cache Follow-Up
summary: Stable Pokemon artwork now receives its intended long-lived cache policy while replaceable team and division logos keep shorter refresh windows.

changes.text: The Pokemon-specific cache header now takes precedence over the general image header, reducing repeat artwork downloads without making replaceable league logos stale.

title: Faster Site, Same Experience
summary: Lossless image compression, leaner data reads, self-hosted fonts, and smarter cache refreshes improve performance without adding hosting cost.

changes.text: Pokemon artwork, sprites, team logos, and division logos use pixel-preserving recompression, reducing bundled PNGs by about 4 MB without changing their URLs or appearance.
Leaderboards and Pokemon Battle Stats reuse fewer database scans and less repeated in-memory work while preserving the same rankings and totals.

Core Web Vitals now use the framework's official measurements, fonts are served with the site instead of requiring an extra stylesheet request, and public data caches refresh immediately after match-result changes.

title: Playoff Eligibility Seeding
summary: Playoff standings now reflect teams marked as ineligible while preserving their regular-season records.

changes.text: Ineligible playoff teams display a red DQ badge, and the next eligible teams move up into the playoff seeds.

title: Coach Strength of Schedule
summary: Coach match history now shows the current strength of schedule for modern seasons.

changes.text: Season 11 and later coach match-history sections now display SOS as the combined win-loss records of scheduled opponents.

title: Replay Attribution, Coach Records & Social Links
summary: More reliable Zoroark move usage, clearer Season 11 coach match records, and centered homepage social links.

changes.text: Zoroark and Hisuian-Zoroark Illusion replay turns now attribute Move Usage to the correct revealed species without duplicate or missing usage during reprocessing.
Season 11 and later coach match history now shows the opponent's win-loss record beside the team name while earlier seasons retain their existing layout.
The homepage now has a centered Connect with PBO social-links row at the top, with the existing footer links preserved.

title: Coach YouTube Playlists
summary: Coach profiles can now show an assigned YouTube playlist, with safe admin assignment and a compact playback experience.

changes.text: Admins can assign or clear a YouTube playlist from Admin → Coaches using a playlist URL or ID.
Coach profiles provide a compact native YouTube player and direct fallback links when playlist data is unavailable.
When YOUTUBE_API_KEY is configured, playlist videos are cached server-side and presented with thumbnails, titles, dates, and click-to-play behavior.

title: Your Week, Connected League Tools
summary: Match prep, schedules, and stats now stay connected to your league context, with clearer weekly actions and mobile controls.

changes.text: Your Week shows match times, opens the correct matchup, and highlights missing pick-ems and their next scheduled lock time.
Carry season, division, week, and team context between schedules, matchup prep, comparisons, and item stats.
Schedule actions are easier to tap on mobile, and stats now offers plain-language discovery links.
Homepage queries fetch only the displayed recent battles and scope trainer type usage to displayed coaches.
Replay Analyzer now validates links early, reports loading and timeout states, supports share/download actions, and limits upstream replay requests safely.

title: Sheet Tab Mapping Sync
summary: Google Sheet team schedule tabs now receive completed results using the spreadsheet's authoritative tab mapping.

changes.text: Match-result sync now resolves team tabs from the Source mapping, preventing abbreviation differences from interrupting normal 0-0 and double-FF updates.

title: Normal 0-0 Team Tab Sync
summary: Normal 0-0 results now update the team schedule tabs and Leaderboards instead of producing a blank result.

changes.text: Completed match sync now writes official W/L values to team schedule tabs, including zero-differential wins and losses that formulas could not infer.

title: Normal 0-0 Result Sync
summary: Normal 0-0 wins now replace stale double-FF differentials in Google Sheet Match Stats and Leaderboards.

changes.text: Completed normal results now write their official differentials to Match Stats, so a 0-0 result remains 0-0 after a previous double-FF value was synced to the fixture.

title: Separate Forfeit Controls
summary: Admins can clearly declare a single FF or a double FF, with double losses synced to Google Sheet leaderboards.

changes.text: Added separate Declare FF and Declare Double FF buttons in the match-result editor.
Declare Double FF clears the winner, applies -3/-3, removes stale game stats, and uses the existing safe Google Sheet sync path; normal completed 0-0 games remain supported separately.

title: Double-Loss Leaderboard Differential
summary: Double-loss official differentials now flow through the Google Sheet leaderboards and games-played totals.

changes.text: Google Sheets Match Stats now writes the official differential for both teams on a double loss, allowing team tabs and Leaderboards to calculate L/L, differential, and GP correctly.

title: Double-Loss Results & Sheet Sync
summary: Admins can record a rule-breaking double loss with a -3 differential for both teams, and the result syncs safely to the Google Sheet.

changes.text: Added double-loss match recording with no winner, a forfeit flag, and independent -3 differentials for both teams.
Google Sheet Match Stats now receives explicit L/L results for double losses while stale Pokemon rows are cleared and Schedule Cutout formulas remain intact.

title: Season 6 Replay Archive
summary: Neon, Sunset, and Stargazer Season 6 replay data is backfilled with current kill attribution and review safeguards.

changes.text: Backfilled supplied Season 6 Neon, Sunset, and Stargazer replays with move usage, explicitly revealed items, battle metrics, replay events, and timestamps.
Season 6 replay K/D and kill-event records now use the current faint-event attribution logic, while roster, result, differential, format, and K/D conflicts are highlighted for review.

title: Overlay Health Bars & Mega Backfill
summary: Health bars align cleanly at every HP value, and Season 11 Mega Stone stats have a guarded roster-aware backfill command.

changes.text: Broadcast overlay health bars now fill flush inside their tracks with consistent borders across the standard, V1, and V2 layouts.
Added a Season 11-only, dry-run-by-default Mega Stone backfill that checks each team roster and transaction history at the match week before inferring a stone.

title: Homepage & Poll Controls
summary: A clearer homepage dashboard and an admin switch for public league polls.

changes.text: Refreshed the homepage hero, season metrics, Quick Actions cards, personalized dashboard styling, and content order for a clearer desktop and mobile experience.
Added separate Admin Poll Controls with a persisted toggle that hides public poll cards without deleting poll questions or vote history.
Quick Actions now prioritize Current Season, Match Prep, Pick-Ems, Fantasy Scout, Free Agency, and PBO Stats, with the hero copy referring to game prep.
Broadcast overlay review and live-state recovery no longer recount the same faint event as an additional Pokemon KO.
Mega Pokemon without an explicitly recorded item now display the corresponding Mega Stone in overlays and match summaries.

title: Season 5 Unova Replay Archive
summary: Season 5 Unova replay history is now attached with guarded review for K/D and Illusion discrepancies.

changes.text: Added all 60 available replays across the complete 63-game Season 5 Unova regular-season and playoff schedule.
Forty-three clean replay games receive replay-derived details, while 17 uncertain games are highlighted yellow with an exact review reason.
Official forfeits no longer count as missing-replay issues, and official PBO winners, differentials, forfeit state, and Pokemon K/D remain unchanged.

title: Replay HAX & Speed Tiers
summary: Clearer replay HAX context and trigger-aware Speed Tiers for current and legacy PBO formats.

changes.text: Replay HAX events now show actual Pokemon species names, exclude guaranteed Fake Out flinches and guaranteed-critical-hit moves, and apply the expanded Season 11 Week 6+ rules through later seasons.

Matchup Prep Speed Tiers now compare grouped calculated speeds against individual base speeds with Rain, Sun, Sand, Snow/Hail, Electric Terrain, Unburden, Quick Feet, Booster Energy, Tailwind, Protosynthesis, Quark Drive, and Slow Start triggers.
Mobile Matchup Prep keeps both rosters visible in compact paired rows and presents a dense PBO-styled tier ladder; desktop retains the wider two-scenario comparison.

title: Replay Review Safeguards
summary: Historical replay imports preserve official PBO results and clearly surface games that need manual review.

changes.text: Admins can hold a match for review with a written reason; held games are highlighted yellow in the match list and editor.
The Season 5 Kalos replay import validates historical formats, scheduled teams, winners, differentials, roster mapping, and PBO kill/death attribution before adding replay-derived details.
Historical imports preserve official PBO winners and Pokemon K/D instead of overwriting discrepancies with raw replay output.

title: Reliable Overlays & Berry Usage
summary: Broadcast battle messages recover reliably, and replay statistics count berries only when they are successfully used.

changes.text: Broadcast Overlay V1 and V2 now restore Showdown animations safely after returning to live play, preventing move and damage messages from remaining hidden.
Berries revealed because Knock Off removed them no longer count as successful berry uses; activated and consumed berries continue to count normally.
Rapid Spin, Defog, and other hazard-removal effects now clear their battlefield sprites reliably instead of leaving stale rocks or spikes visible.
Live overlays now skip throttled background-tab animations when brought back into view or when Go Live is selected, while preserving the complete turn history for review.

title: On-Demand Website Hosting
summary: The website can sleep during quiet periods again while retaining the new health and deployment safeguards.

changes.text: Fly can stop the production machine when it is unused and automatically wake it for the next visitor, reducing always-on hosting costs while preserving database-backed health checks.

title: Faster, Safer Website Releases
summary: Health checks, controlled database migrations, automated release checks, and smaller assets make the website more dependable.

changes.text: The production website verifies database health before receiving traffic, applies tracked indexes once before startup, and ships through automated code, build, and asset checks.
Oversized team and division logos and the production container are optimized for faster deployments without changing their public URLs.

title: Instant Store Cosmetics
summary: Purchased cosmetics now appear immediately and color cosmetics always have a visible default.

changes.text: Store purchases, activation changes, and color updates now refresh cosmetic displays immediately, while color cosmetics use the Stargazer preset until a coach chooses another color.

title: Historical Match Stat Corrections
summary: Admins can accurately correct Pokemon appearances and K/D records for historical matches.

changes.text: Season 5-9 match result editors can select any Pokemon in the database when correcting historical stats, while other seasons remain restricted to team rosters.

title: Faster Matchup Selection
summary: Matchup Prep now loads schedule choices in smaller, faster steps.

changes.text: Selecting a division now loads only its week numbers, and selecting a week loads only that week's matchups instead of the full division schedule.

title: Coach Milestone Cache Follow-Up
summary: Coach record milestones now reuse their large shared source dataset without exceeding the framework cache-item limit.

changes.text: The shared coach-milestone dataset now uses a bounded 60-second server-process cache, avoiding repeated record queries and oversized framework-cache warnings.

title: Divisional Records & Move Sources
summary: Season 6+ divisional record books, linked coach achievements, richer Move Usage sources, and faster record pages.

changes.text: Battle Record now has official-color record pages for Infinity, Stargazer, Sunset, Crystal, and Neon with Overall, Regular Season, and Playoffs scopes covering Season 6 onward.
Top-three PBO and divisional record holders receive coach milestone titles that link directly to the applicable record page.
Move Usage rows can lazily load game sources with matchup, coach, move-count, match, and replay context.
Short-lived caches and targeted database indexes speed up Battle Record, coach milestones, and Move Usage sources while keeping recent results fresh.
Move Usage appearance totals retain games with an empty saved move map and clearly identify them as having no recorded move commands.

title: Current Stats & Faster Public Pages
summary: Current-season leaderboards, match data-quality tools, and faster public page data paths.

changes.text: Leaderboards can switch between the current season and all-time coach and Pokemon statistics.
Admins have a Data Quality review queue for missing deciding turns, replay links, Pokemon rows, and invalid winners.
Homepage, leaderboard, season, and coach public datasets now use short-lived caching while account-specific content remains dynamic.
Season and coach queries now fetch scoped rows, leaderboard scopes share one Pokemon-stat scan, and targeted indexes accelerate common public reads.
The homepage column layout now uses CSS instead of browser resize observers and synchronization state.

title: New Logo Frames
summary: Three new animated and themed logo frames are available in the PBO Store.

changes.text: Inferno, Icy, and Chromatic Flow logo frames are now available for 375 PBO Coins each.

title: Team Name Comparison Search
summary: Coach comparisons are now easier to find by franchise name.

changes.text: The coach comparison picker now lists and searches the latest team names in alphabetical order while preserving career coach records.

title: Automatic Release Notes
summary: Website deployments and release notes now ship as one guarded workflow.

changes.text: Every Fly deployment must include a uniquely keyed changelog entry dated for that Pacific-time day, and the server synchronizes it automatically during startup.

title: Stats, Comparisons & Changelog
summary: A full statistics integrity pass, new comparison tools, clearer replay reports, and a deployment-backed website changelog.

changes.text: Compare up to four coaches or Pokemon with shareable season, division, match-phase, and forfeit filters.
Admins can create, edit, publish, draft, and delete categorized website updates from the new Changelog editor.
Coach records can switch between Overall, Regular Season, and Playoffs, while the comprehensive Pokemon leaderboard now includes wins and losses.
Match replays have a clearer visual hierarchy and separate Favorable Crits, Flinches, Missed Moves, and HAX Count statistics.
A Seasons 5-11 audit corrected invalid or orphaned stat rows, record calculations, revealed-item handling, and stale fantasy cache totals.
Battle Record calculations now reject malformed winners, apply the official Season 6 differential rule, and use qualifying matches for consecutive-season records.

title: Stats & Sharing Updates
summary: Expanded career records, clearer coach profiles, and richer Pokemon battle statistics.

changes.text: PBO Records now includes Overall, Regular Season, and Playoffs career records for wins, losses, and matches played.
Pokemon Battle Stats now includes Kills and Deaths leaderboards with Total and Per Game views.
Coach profiles keep overall records visible while Regular Season, Playoffs, and Revealed Item Tendencies can be expanded when needed.
Game Prep and PBO Stats navigation groups now organize their related tools in focused dropdown menus.
The retired 5-Match Survival Streak milestone is no longer generated or delivered.

title: Season 11 Fun Facts
summary: Public fun-fact records and the playoff projection tool now reflect the current league format.

changes.text: Pokemon and coach fun-fact pages now calculate and label their records from Season 11.
The playoff calculator uses the shared PBO ELO expected-score formula for matchup probabilities.
The Pokemon fun-facts cache was versioned so deployments cannot briefly reuse Season 10 results.

title: Readability & Match Prep
summary: A round of usability improvements for public pages on desktop and mobile.

changes.text: Selected Match Prep teams now show their completed division record beside the coach name.
Dense public-page metadata is larger and shared retro buttons provide a 44px minimum touch target.
Infinity standings and Fantasy leaderboard colors now handle saved division names consistently.
